# Merge patch JSON (RFC 7386)

Dans le répertoire courant, crée `merge_patch.py`.

## Interface

```bash
python3 merge_patch.py <target.json> <patch.json>
```

Affiche sur stdout le JSON résultant de l'application du patch sur la cible,
et rien d'autre. Sortie avec un code non nul et un message sur stderr si un
fichier est illisible ou contient un JSON invalide.

## Sémantique RFC 7386

- Si le patch n'est pas un objet, il remplace entièrement la cible.
- Si le patch est un objet :
  - une valeur `null` supprime la clé correspondante ;
  - une valeur objet est fusionnée récursivement avec la valeur existante
    (si l'existante n'est pas un objet, elle est remplacée par un objet vide
    avant la fusion) ;
  - toute autre valeur remplace la valeur existante.
- Le résultat conserve les clés de la cible absentes du patch.
- Les entrées d'un tableau sont remplacées en bloc, jamais fusionnées.
- Les fichiers d'entrée ne doivent pas être modifiés.

## Contraintes

- Bibliothèque standard uniquement.
- Ne crée aucun autre fichier.
- Les objets doivent préserver l'ordre d'insertion (les clés de la cible
  d'abord, puis les nouvelles clés du patch).

tools.description:
Read several files in one call. Use it instead of several `read_file` calls when
the files are independent. Paths are relative to the workspace or absolute
inside it. Each file is truncated to `max_lines` with a marker. Binary files
and unreadable paths are reported per file instead of failing the whole call.
tools.name: read_files

tools.description:
Return a compact skeleton of a source file: imports and the signatures of its
classes, functions and methods, each with its line number. Use it before
`read_file` on a large file to decide which ranges to read. Supports Python,
JavaScript, TypeScript, Go, Rust, Java, C/C++ and Ruby; other files fall back to
a head. Never returns the whole file.
tools.name: index

tools.description:
Find files by glob pattern inside the workspace, for example `**/*.py` or
`src/**/*.ts`. Excludes .git, virtualenvs, node_modules, caches and build
directories. Returns paths relative to the workspace, sorted.

pattern.description: Glob pattern relative to the workspace
pattern.title: Pattern

tools.name: glob

tools.description:
Apply several exact string replacements to one file atomically. Provide the
edits in order; each `old_string` must match exactly once unless `replace_all`
is true. If any edit fails, no change is written. Prefer this over several
`edit` calls on the same file.
tools.name: multiedit

- Issue independent tool calls in the same turn instead of one per turn.
- Prefer one shell command that checks several things over several commands.
- Never read the same file twice. After an edit, verify with the project's test, not a full re-read.
- Finish simple tasks in as few turns as possible. Do not narrate between tool calls.

# Verification
- Verify each change by running the relevant test or command. Do not claim success without it.
- Same error twice: stop, re-read the failing code or output, change approach.
- If the task is ambiguous, ask one concrete question instead of guessing.

# Professional objectivity
Prioritize technical accuracy over agreeing. Disagree when needed; do not flatter.

Summarize what changed and how it was verified, in a few lines.
